observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly reorders operators with the same precedence (specifically *, /, and %), leading to incorrect associativity and invalid code generation.
reasoning_summary: The bug involves incorrect handling of operator associativity for operators with the same precedence level. This is a procedural logic error in the code generation/printing phase where the compiler incorrectly reorders expressions. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object). It is a flaw in the implementation of the expression printing/reordering algorithm.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'As *, / and % all have the same operator precedence they should be left-to-right, but hoisting the 2 to the beginning means it's on the wrong side of the modulus operator.'
Triggering tests show failures in associativity: 'expected:<var a,b,c;a||[(b||c);a*(b*c);a|(b|c)]> but was:<var a,b,c;a||[b||c;a*b*c;a|b|c]>'
Triggering tests show failures in associativity: 'expected:<3*[(4%3*5)]> but was:<3*[4%3*5]>'
PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntaxTest::testAssocitivity fails, indicating the peephole optimization logic is incorrectly reordering associative operators.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a missing guard or validation check, but an incorrect implementation of the operator associativity logic.
While it involves the relationship between operators, the root cause is the incorrect implementation of the associativity algorithm itself, not a broken association between separate modules.
